sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 18.12.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Ram Rawat, learned counsel and Shri Indra Deo Mishra,
learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant and the victim are neighbours.
2. The victims had asked the applicant to purchase a mobile phone for them from the market.
The applicant did their bidding on account of the long standing family relationship between the parties.
3. The innocent gesture of the applicant has been misconstrued and false and aggravated allegations have been made in the FIR.

4. The victims have not made any allegation of abduction, commission of rape or inappropriate sexual conduct by the applicant in the FIR or in their statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
5.
Some false and aggravated allegations were made by the victims in their statements under Section 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents to save the failing prosecution case.
6. Material inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements of the victims under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
7. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victims has not been produced by the prosecution.
8. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
9. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Arvind Anuragi be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties, or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
